nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: Prior to synthesis, the Ni foams (1 × 2 cm²) were ultrasonically cleaned with 3 M HCl, acetone, ethanol and deionized (DI) water for 10 min each to removed unwanted impurities.

nodes.name: Chemical bath deposition and annealing
nodes.procedure: 0.1 M Fe(NO₃)₂·9H₂O, 0.1 M Na₂MoO₄, and 0.24 M CH₄N₂O were mixed in 60 mL DI water under magnetic stirring for 15 min. The resulting recipe was transferred into a 100 mL glass bottle with a piece of Ni foam immersed in the reaction solution, and the glass bottle was placed in hot air oven and then maintained at 100 °C for 6 h at a heating rate of 2 °C min⁻¹. After natural cooling, the material loaded Ni foam was taken out, washed with DI water and ethanol and then dried at 60 °C for overnight. Finally, the electrodes were sintered at 200 °C for 2 h in air at a heating rate of 2 °C min⁻¹. The average mass of FeMoO₄ HNSAs electrode material on Ni foam was found to be ∼2.9 mg cm⁻².

nodes.description: Battery-type performance as positive electrode in 3 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the FeMoO4 HNSAs electrode exhibits superior electrochemical performances with a high specific capacity (∼158.39 mA h g−1 at 2 A g−1), excellent rate capability (∼88.08% retains even at 8 A g−1⋅), and outstanding cycling life (∼90.76% at 6 A g−1 over 4000 cycles)

nodes.description: Pseudocapacitive performance as negative electrode in 3 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the FeMoO4 HNSAs achieves a high specific capacitance of 477.47 F g−1 at 2 A g−1, excellent rate capability of 95.54% even at 8 A g−1, and superior cycling stability with 92.37% capacity retention after 4000 cycles at 6 A g−1

nodes.description: EIS characterization in 3 M KOH three-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: The FeMoO4 HNSAs electrode delivers smaller Rs (0.34 Ω cm2) and Rct (2.34 Ω cm2) values, denoting high electrical conductivity and rapid charge transfer.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms β-FeMoO4 phase with diffraction peaks at 2θ = 12.9°, 23.0°, 25.0°, 26.2°, 31.7°, 36.3°, and 39.8° corresponding to (−110), (021), (201), (−220), (112), (400) and (−330) planes (JCPDS No. 22-0628).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction peaks at 2θ = 12.9°, 23.0°, 25.0°, 26.2°, 31.7°, 36.3°, and 39.8° are well identified as (−110), (021), (201), (−220), (112), (400) and (−330) planes of β-FeMoO4 (JCPDS No. 22-0628), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Fe, Mo, O (and Ni from substrate); Fe 2p shows Fe²⁺ at 707.89/723.14 eV, Fe³⁺ at 712.84/725.83 eV (sat. 718.0 eV); Mo 3d shows Mo⁶⁺ (3d₃/₂ 235.22 eV, 3d₅/₂ 232.06 eV, ΔE=3.16 eV); O 1s at 529.91 eV (M-O), 531.12 eV (lattice O), 532.10 eV (adsorbed H₂O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Fig. 2a, the full-survey-scan spectrum shows the existence of Ni, Fe, Mo, O, and C elements ... the peaks at 707.89 and 723.14 eV indicate Fe²⁺, while the peaks at 712.84 and 725.83 eV are assigned to Fe³⁺ ... For the Mo 3d spectra (Fig. 2c), the main two peaks of Mo 3d₃/₂ (235.22 eV) and Mo 3d₅/₂ (232.06 eV) ... The peaks observed at binding energies of 529.91 eV (O1), 531.12 eV (O2) and 532.10 eV (O3).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals honeycomb-like microstructure of interconnected ultrathin nanosheets with uniform thickness of ~35 nm covering entire Ni foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the increased magnification as shown in Fig. 2(b) and (c), it can be seen that the FeMoO4 material forms a well-defined honeycomb-like microstructure composed of interconnected ultrathin nanosheets with a relatively uniform thickness of ~35 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM-EDX color mapping confirms homogeneous distribution of Fe, Mo and O elements in FeMoO4 HNSAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM-EDX color mapping was carried out to examine the distribution of elements in the FeMoO4 HNSAs. The mapping images shown in Fig. 3d clearly revealed the homogeneous distribution of Fe, Mo and O elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms honeycomb-like structures assembled by interconnected nanosheet arrays with thinner nanosheet thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in TEM images of Fig. 4(a) and (b), it is remarkable that the FeMoO4 honeycomb-like structures are assembled by interconnected nanosheet arrays. The high-magnification TEM image shown in Fig. 4c indicates the thinner thickness of the typical FeMoO4 HNSAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.34 nm corresponding to the (−220) crystal plane of β-FeMoO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image shown in Fig. 4d, the lattice spring of 0.34 nm can be related to the (−220) crystal plane of β-FeMoO4.
